subject.title: Foothill Municipal Water District Board, Division 5

text: As a Water Resource Specialist at the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, I spend my days working on solving the most difficult water problems throughout the region. I began my decade-long career in the water sector after graduating from the University of California, Berkeley with a degree in Environmental Economics. My husband and I have lived in the Foothill region for over six years. We cherish the Foothill community, and look forward to many more years here.

With the growing impacts of climate change, it is critical that our community develops infrastructure and supply management plans for responding to both emergencies and drought periods. These plans must be financially prudent and respect the rate-payers who fund them. My professional and personal experience has prepared me to navigate the complex economic, political, and legal challenges facing the Foothill Municipal Water District Board. My goal is to ensure safe, reliable, and equitable access to water at the lowest cost for the residents of the Foothill region.
I humbly request your support as I seek to serve you on the Foothill Municipal Water District Board and guide our community to dependable and cost effective access to water for years to come.

text: Hi, I am running for Foothill Municipal Water District (FMWD) Board because the Eaton fire showed how much is at stake. FMWD serves Altadena, La Cañada Flintridge, and La Crescenta. La Crescenta was spared from last January's fires; next time we may not be, and the recovery next door has been far too slow. I grew up in this community, am raising my two daughters here and have almost two decades of experience in water management and infrastructure financing. Currently, I lead the innovation program for one of the world's largest water utilities. If elected, I will focus on three priorities. First, coordinate more proactively with first responders on future disasters and speed up the Altadena fire recovery. Second, invest in local water supplies like water recycling and stormwater recharge to save ratepayer money. Third, stop letting paperwork block progress. I bring an insider's knowledge of how water agencies work, but an outsider's mind for how they should work better, faster, and cheaper. Last year's fires exposed real failures, but I firmly believe that together we can turn this breakdown into a breakthrough. Learn more at: https://bit.ly/future_of_the_foothills
